claims.text: The PGM nanoscale catalyst has superior activity, selectivity, and durability during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic fluctuations in the catalyst's surface oxidation state govern its activity, selectivity, and durability during ethanol oxidation.
Surface oxidation-state fluctuations tune the adsorption energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Changing ambient oxygen partial pressure modulates the surface oxidation state of the PGM catalyst.
Standard ambient oxygen produces a surface oxidation state that optimizes intermediate binding.
Oxygen partial pressures above or below the ambient baseline cause measurable declines in catalytic performance.
The catalyst's surface oxidation state influences its d-band center.
Changes in the catalyst's d-band center modulate the binding energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Departures from ambient oxygen disrupt the optimal adsorption balance and shift voltammetric signatures.
At ambient oxygen partial pressure, the catalyst will exhibit distinct voltammetric peaks and high turnover frequencies.
Increasing or decreasing oxygen relative to ambient will systematically shift electrochemical signatures and reduce ethanol-oxidation activity and selectivity.
The proposed mechanism operates only within an electrochemical potential window that permits dynamic modulation of the surface oxidation state.
Extremely reducing or oxidizing potentials override dynamic surface oxidation-state modulation and cause the proposed mechanism to fail.
The magnitude of oxygen-dependent performance changes may depend on reaction temperature and electrolyte composition.
